chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Is ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a slave who claimed to be free, but did not bring proof for that; should I buy him? He said, 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying a slave who claims to be free but has no proof?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that a slave who claims freedom (*mudakkir* or *mukattib* context) without bringing proof should still be purchased, reflecting the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) where the status of slavery remains until proven otherwise. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for determining ownership transfer and the financial responsibility of the buyer in cases of disputed emancipation, ensuring commercial stability by not halting transactions due to unverified claims.
